latest_clarification: Every item in the Subject graph is an Entity, including a Node, Atom.Status Property and a CFEL Relation. This does not itself settle a root branch or declare a new kind.

evidence.finding: Current @5 lexical Entity Term is active. Its Claim describes a common category for primary graph nodes and dependent properties and explicitly introduces Term//Entity. Its Semantics/Details also assert an Entity root and contain stale pending-Draft/staging material; those assertions conflict with the later retirement direction and cannot decide the pending root question.

Current @32 defines Subject Path as identifying one addressed thing or topic, but still asserts Entity as root under R2462. Current R2462 actually declares Node, so this root citation is stale; later human clarification expands what is called Entity, without establishing that stale structural claim.

Relation is a directed Relation Type; declared model Entities or instances, including CFEL descriptors, can be endpoints. Direct and derived Relation descriptors are distinct Relations; literal values and glyphs are not endpoints. Relation name/token is not automatically its descriptor identity.

Its formal selectors (Node, Node.**) cover primary Node and dependent Property and allow HAS_PROPERTY on those model entities; this evidence does not prove all CFEL Relation descriptors are Node instances or carry the same permissions.
Atom.Header.Status is an authored qualified Property Subject; the clarified general Entity term may refer to that Property as a graph entity, without converting status values into graph entities.

Current rule governs old Entity Subject and states every Entity may bear >=0 Property occurrences, with Entity-to-Property HAS_PROPERTY formal relation. Current subject Entity/Property and use of Entity as formal selector need reconciliation with the pending root decision and relation endpoint/permission authorities.

scope_options_without_asserting_new_synt.evidence: An ordinary-language Rule can describe all Subject-graph entities in its Claim while keeping lexical Term//Entity distinct from a modeled root. The active Subject must still have an existing target whose scope truthfully owns this rule; no such universal target has yet been established by this audit.
scope_options_without_asserting_new_synt.limit: Prose does not by itself supply a CFEL-wide universal selector or HAS_PROPERTY endpoint permission.

scope_options_without_asserting_new_synt.evidence: Use an existing proven selector such as (Node, Node.**) for its evidenced subset, and separately govern other applicable declared targets only where their own endpoint permissions and scope are established.
scope_options_without_asserting_new_synt.limit: The Node subset is not established as the full Subject universe; do not silently exclude CFEL Relation descriptors or add permissions.

first_gap_after_pending_answer: If Entity is lexical-only, identify an existing active Subject that truly governs the whole Subject-graph universe and an admitted formal selector/endpoint domain covering every intended entity, or retain a prose-only scoped rule and explicit unresolved formal coverage. If Entity is a structural root, establish the authoritative declaration, membership/identity and relation permissions before revising R1259. No new root, kind, universal syntax or automatic Relation Property permission is inferred.
limits: Source-only; no Workbench/Workflow, code, tests, Git or canonical mutation.
Prior M451 retirement plan is not proof of retirement; live M451@5 is Active.
